Customer-provided workload profile (from Prod traces & interviews):
- Primary workloads: customer-support chat (stateful), fraud-reranking pipeline (batch/hybrid), embeddings for search indexing.
- Observed steady-state QPS: ~18 requests/sec for chat (avg payload ~140 tokens per request).
- Observed peak burst (marketing campaign / payroll run): up to 110 requests/sec sustained for ~7 minutes; short spikes to ~220 rps for <30s.
- Reranker jobs: scheduled batch windows produce 3000 concurrent lightweight requests over 15m; per-request size ~60 tokens.
- Embedding throughput: background 5k requests/day; occasional warm-up indexing 25k reqs in 1 hour.

Internal targets & SLO asks (customer):
- Chat p50 latency <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms (token stream acceptable), p99 target <= 350ms or automatic fallback.
- Reranker p95 <= 150ms; batch throughput must finish within scheduled window (30m SLA).
- Embeddings p95 <= 120ms for interactive reindex calls.
- Availability SLA: 99.95% for production endpoints; incident response (P1) within 1 hour.
- Credits/penalty negotiation expected for >30m downtime.

Baseline sizing assumptions (workshop pre-read):
- Average chat request ~140 tokens => steady-state token/sec ~= 18 rps * 140 = 2520 tok/s. Peak sustained ~= 110 * 140 = 15400 tok/s. Burst peak brief ~= 220 * 140 = 30800 tok/s.
- Reranker steady tokens/sec (during window) ~= 3000 * 60 tokens / 900s = ~200 tok/s sustained across the window; but concurrency requires handling 3k parallel lightweight inferences.
- Reserve planning: recommend a mix of reserved H100-equivalent slots for chat (low-latency) + dedicated A100 pool for throughput-heavy reranking/embeddings.
- Suggested redundancy: N+1 across two AZs to meet 99.95% target and permit rolling upgrades.

Open negotiation points / questions: 
- Exact GPU SKU preference (H100 vs A100) and quantization acceptance for certain models. Meridian prefers H100 for latency but is cost sensitive.
- Can Redwood guarantee burst capacity without immediate overage costs? Need defined burst buffer policy and failover to slightly cheaper model variant.
- SLA credit definitions (measurement windows, maintenance exclusions).
- Network egress and VPC peering throughput limits — Meridian's infra team requires baseline throughput test plan.
